title: Thread Contention on Coarse-Grained Locks
pattern: Protecting high-frequency, read-mostly operations using a single global or coarse-grained execution lock.
why_bad: It forces parallel execution paths to serialize, incurring massive cache miss latency and lock-acquisition-induced context switches (lock bouncing).
detection: Global mutexes (`Mutex` or `spin_lock`) acquired in non-mutating search or read-mostly operations.
counterexample: The system only runs on a single-core CPU where lock contention cannot occur. `Contextual`.
fix: Use fine-grained bucket locking, read-write locks (`RwLock`), hazard pointers, or RCU (Read-Copy Update).
source: *1701.00854v6.pdf*, Chapter 10 (p. 8 / p. 9) and *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 175).
